**Studron's budget is $2,590K.**

Only Finance Office entries change the budget. Messages from every other source were ignored. The figure is the #0001 starting value of $1,870K plus the net of all Finance changes still in effect, which comes to +$720K. I added this once by hand and did not run an independent second pass.

**How I handled withdrawals.** A withdrawal only counts if it has not itself been withdrawn, so I traced each chain to its last link. Four chains show the pattern:
- **#0006 (−$77K) stays in effect.** It was targeted by #0008, which #0013 withdrew; #0031 withdrew #0013, and #0066 withdrew #0031. #0066 is the final, effective link, so #0013 stands and #0008 does not.
- **#0004 (+$27K) is removed.** Its chain runs #0011 → #0018 → #0021 → #0102 → #0107 → #0472 → #0522. #0522 is effective, so #0107 stands, which leaves #0021 and #0011 in effect, which removes #0004.
- **#0026 (+$473K) is removed.** Its chain runs #0040 → #0115 → #0171 → #0567 → #0267. Working back from #0267, #0040 stands.
- **#0103 (+$52K) stays in effect.** Its chain runs #0337 → #0740 → #1352 → #1463. Working back from #1463, #0740 stands, so #0337 is cancelled.

After resolving every chain this way, about 120 Finance updates are withdrawn. Some examples are #0004, #0014, #0022, #0026, #0032, #0036, #0069, #0100, #0127, #0157, #0484, #0493, #0684, #1114, #1324 and #1335. All other Finance increases and decreases apply once, in order.
